deals.evidence: Tanenbaum announced Monday he is selling a 20-per-cent stake in his company, Kilmer Sports Inc., to OMERS for US$400 million.
deals.headline: OMERS buys 5% indirect stake in MLSE from Tanenbaum for US$400M
deals.summary: Ontario pension plan OMERS bought 20% of Tanenbaum's Kilmer Sports Inc., which owned 25% of MLSE, for US$400 million, an indirect 5% of MLSE, as a financial investor with no operational role.

deals.evidence: today announced it has signed an agreement to buy Bell’s 37.5% ownership stake in Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment (MLSE) for C$4.7 billion
deals.headline: Rogers buys Bell's 37.5% of MLSE for C$4.7bn
deals.summary: Rogers agreed to buy Bell's 37.5% of MLSE for C$4.7 billion (about US$3.5 billion per SBJ), taking it to 75%; funded mainly from revolving bank credit facilities and cash on hand.

deals.evidence: Rogers acquired the remaining 25% ownership stake in MLSE from Kilmer Sports Inc. for C$4.35 billion
deals.headline: Rogers buys Kilmer's last 25% of MLSE for C$4.35bn, becoming sole owner
deals.seller: Kilmer Sports Inc. (Larry Tanenbaum; OMERS indirect holder)
deals.summary: Rogers acquired the remaining 25% of MLSE from Kilmer Sports Inc. for C$4.35 billion, financed from committed liquidity, taking its ownership to 100%; Rogers plans a new Rogers Sports unit and to sell a minority stake in its sports, media and entertainment assets.

name: Toronto Maple Leafs Hockey Club
notes: Revenue, operating income (EBITDA) and player expenses are Forbes estimates for 2024-25 (USD, net of revenue sharing and arena debt service); valuation is Forbes enterprise value calculated December 2025, before Rogers completed its buyout (Forbes still lists Rogers Communications and Larry Tanenbaum; purchased 2012 and 1996). Rogers' 37.5% dates from the 2012 purchase of Ontario Teachers' 80% with Bell (Sportico 2023: 'Rogers Communications and Bell Canada acquired the other 75%'); Kilmer went from 20.5% to 25% then. The 2023 Sportico report put the OMERS deal at an enterprise value of more than $8 billion (pre-signing report), so no valuation is set on that deal. The Rogers-Kilmer deal values all MLSE (Leafs, Raptors, TFC, Argonauts, Scotiabank Arena), not the Leafs alone. Chair after the buyout is not stated on a page read (Tanenbaum was chairman). Missing: arena capacity (scotiabankarena.com blocks automated reads), social, attendance, sponsors, chair.

owners.evidence: increasing its ownership of MLSE to 100%
owners.name: Rogers Communications Inc.

ownership_summary: Owned by Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment (MLSE), which since October 1, 2026 is 100% owned by Rogers Communications Inc. (TSX/NYSE-listed). Rogers held 37.5% from 2012, bought Bell/BCE's 37.5% (closed July 2025) and then Kilmer Sports' (Larry Tanenbaum's) remaining 25% for C$4.35 billion; OMERS' indirect interest through Kilmer (bought 2023) went with that sale. Rogers has said it intends to sell a minority stake in its consolidated sports, media and entertainment assets.
